description: GHWR, a multi-method global heatwave and warm-spell record and toolbox is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Ehsan Raei et al. Heatwaves are extended periods of unusually high temperatures with significant societal and environmental impacts. Despite their significance, there is not a generalized definition for heatwaves. In this paper, we introduce a multi-method global heatwave and warm-spell data record and analysis toolbox (named GHWR). Coverage: global; published in 2018. The formats are not stated in the sources read. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC BY 4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
